holidays.name: National Grilled Cheese Sandwich Day
holidays.description: A gooey, golden-brown celebration of bread, butter, and melted cheese. Home cooks and diners across America honor the humble sandwich with extra-stretchy cheese pulls.
holidays.origin: Observed in the United States as a food holiday, with the date popularly set on April 12. Its exact founder is unclear, but it is widely promoted by cheese and restaurant brands.
holidays.funFact: The grilled cheese took off in the 1920s when sliced bread and processed cheese became widely available, and the U.S. Navy served them to sailors during World War II.

holidays.name: International Day of Human Space Flight
holidays.description: A United Nations observance celebrating humanity's journey into the cosmos, honoring astronauts, cosmonauts, and the dreamers who look up and say, 'Let's go there.'
holidays.origin: Established by the UN General Assembly in 2011 to mark the anniversary of Yuri Gagarin's historic orbit of Earth on April 12, 1961, aboard Vostok 1.
holidays.funFact: Gagarin's flight lasted only about 108 minutes, yet it made him the first human in space and a global celebrity overnight.

holidays.name: Walk on Stilts Day
holidays.description: An unofficial holiday inviting people to strap on some height and see the world from a few feet higher. Expect wobbles, laughter, and questionable decisions about ceiling fans.
holidays.origin: A lighthearted unofficial observance listed in quirky holiday calendars, celebrating the age-old art of stilt walking.
holidays.funFact: Shepherds in France's Landes region once walked on tall stilts to cross marshy land and keep watch over their flocks.

holidays.name: National Licorice Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of the polarizing chewy candy, whether you prefer classic black twists or red ropes that argue they're not really licorice at all.
holidays.origin: A food-calendar observance in the United States dedicated to the candy made from the root of the licorice plant.
holidays.funFact: Real licorice root contains glycyrrhizin, which is about 50 times sweeter than sugar, and eating too much can actually raise blood pressure.

holidays.name: Look Up at the Sky Day
holidays.description: A gentle reminder to stop staring at your phone and tilt your chin skyward to appreciate clouds, stars, birds, and whatever else is up there.
holidays.origin: An informal observance, often tied to April 12 as a nod to the space-flight anniversary and the joy of sky-watching.
holidays.funFact: Cloud-watching even has a dedicated group, the Cloud Appreciation Society, which has tens of thousands of members worldwide.
